observed_title: On the extreme points of moments sets
version: arXiv:1204.0249v1; manuscript dated October 31, 2018; 10 PDF pages.

read_ranges.scope: Read the complete extracted text, including definitions, all proofs, topological corollaries, discussion, and references. Rendered PDF pages 2, 4, 6, and 8 to inspect the moment-vector, finite-atom, and Polish-space formulas.

topic_relevance.A03: adjacent: characterizes extreme points and finite-atom representations of generalized moment sets, and lists compactness conditions that ensure an extreme maximizer exists. It does not prove tightness of near-extremizing sequences or analyze concentration/mass escape.

definitions.name: Generalized moment set
definitions.statement: For measurable f=(f₁,…,f_k) and C⊂R^k, M_{f,C} consists of nonnegative measures μ with f∈L¹(μ) and ∫f dμ∈C; Λ_{f,C}=Λ∩M_{f,C}.

definitions.name: μ-atoms and atomic partitions
definitions.statement: A is a μ-atom when every measurable B has μ(A∩B) equal to either 0 or μ(A). An atomic non-null partition divides S into disjoint μ-atoms of positive mass.

definitions.name: Restriction-stable cone hypothesis
definitions.statement: The theorem assumes Λ is a convex cone closed under measurable restrictions μ↦μ_A.

definitions.name: Extreme point
definitions.statement: μ∈ex K when every representation μ=(1−t)ν₀+tν₁ with t∈(0,1) and ν₀,ν₁∈K has ν₀=ν₁.

definitions.name: Finite atomic class Δ_f^(k)
definitions.statement: The paper’s Δ_f^(k) consists of measures with at most k positive Dirac weights whose f-values at support points are linearly independent; Δ^(k) allows up to k nonnegative weights without that independence condition.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 1 (necessary atomic-partition condition for extreme moment measures)
assumptions: C⊂R^k; Λ is a convex cone closed under measurable restrictions μ↦μ_A.
μ is a nonzero extreme point of Λ_{f,C}.
The generalized moments ∫f dμ exist as required by membership in Λ_{f,C}.
theorem_cards.statement: There is an atomic non-null partition of S into m≤k pieces such that the moment vectors ∫_{A_i} f dμ are linearly independent.
proof_steps: 作者证明：if a positive-mass partition had n>k pieces, its n moment vectors in R^k would be linearly dependent.

作者证明：choose a nonzero dependence ε and define ν±=Σ_i(1±ε_i)μ_{A_i}; the restriction-stable cone keeps ν± in Λ, the moment dependence keeps them in the same moment set, and μ=(ν++ν−)/2 with ν+≠ν−, contradicting extremality.

作者证明：take a maximal number m of positive-mass partition pieces. It cannot exceed k; if any piece were not a μ-atom, splitting it would produce m+1 pieces, a contradiction. The moment vectors are independent by the same perturbation argument.
核验基础推导：the convex decomposition and moment-preservation identities follow directly from the linear dependence and restriction operation; the bound m≤k is the dimension bound in R^k.
gaps: This is a structural characterization of extreme points, not a compactness theorem or a statement about arbitrary near-extremizing sequences.

theorem_cards.label: Corollary 4 (finite-atom representation preserving moments and objective)
assumptions: For a chosen measurable g, ∫g dμ exists for each μ∈Λ_{f,C}.
For membership of the representative in Λ itself, additionally require Δ_f^(k)⊂Λ.
theorem_cards.statement: For every extreme μ∈Λ_{f,C}, some measure μ̃ with at most k atoms has the same generalized moments and the same integral of g. With Δ_f^(k)⊂Λ, μ̃ also belongs to Λ_{f,C}. The representation need not mean μ itself is atomic on an abstract measurable space.
proof_steps: 作者证明：Theorem 1 gives an atomic partition with ≤k pieces and independent moment vectors.
作者证明：on each μ-atom, Lemma 3 makes every f_j and g constant μ-a.e.; choose a representative point s_i from the full-measure intersection and set μ̃=Σ_i μ(A_i)δ_{s_i}.
作者证明：the selected values preserve each ∫f_j dμ and ∫g dμ; the extra inclusion Δ_f^(k)⊂Λ yields feasible membership.
核验基础推导：the coefficients μ(A_i) are nonnegative and sum to μ(S); when total mass is among the fixed moment constraints, mass is preserved as well.
gaps: Without the additional Δ inclusion, the paper proves preservation of moments/objective but not membership in Λ. For abstract measurable spaces, the result is a representing measure, not equality with μ.

theorem_cards.label: Corollary 5 and Proposition 6 (reduction of a supremum to finite-atom measures)
assumptions: Condition (2): Λ is a convex cone closed under restrictions.
The supremum of ∫g over Λ_{f,C} equals the supremum over its extreme points.
For equality with feasible finite-atom measures, also assume Δ_f^(k)⊂Λ. Proposition 6 lists sufficient cases, including a nonempty compact convex maximizing face in a locally convex topology.
theorem_cards.statement: Under the extreme-point supremum condition, the supremum over Λ_{f,C} is bounded above by the supremum over at-most-k-atom moment representatives; with Δ_f^(k)⊂Λ, the suprema are equal. A nonempty compact convex maximizing set is one sufficient route to an extreme maximizer and hence to that extreme-point condition.
proof_steps: 作者证明：Corollary 4 sends each extreme maximizer to a finite-atom representative preserving the objective; equality of the supremum over all measures and extreme points gives the upper bound.
作者证明：when Δ_f^(k)⊂Λ, the finite-atom competitors are feasible, giving the reverse inequality.
作者援引：compactness of a convex maximizing face yields an extreme point by Krein–Milman; some other Proposition 6 cases rely on the cited literature.
核验基础推导：the equality needs the stated inclusion and attainment/extreme-point premise; it does not follow from finite-atom representability alone.
gaps: The paper does not guarantee that a maximizing face is compact/nonempty in a given application; these are external hypotheses to check. Equality of suprema does not imply every maximizing sequence has a convergent subsequence.

theorem_cards.label: Corollary 11 (literal atomicity in Polish Borel spaces)
assumptions: S is Polish, Σ is its Borel σ-algebra, and Λ is the cone of all nonnegative measures M.
The moment set fixes a singleton generalized moment value c∈R^k.
theorem_cards.statement: The extreme points of Λ_{f,c} are exactly the feasible measures in Δ_f^(k); under these topological assumptions, the extreme measure itself is k-atomic rather than merely represented by one.
proof_steps: 作者证明：Corollary 10 identifies μ-atoms with point masses under the Polish/Borel/Radon hypotheses.
作者推论：combine Corollary 10 with the necessary Theorem 1 and sufficient Theorem 7.
核验基础推导：this conclusion depends on all the topological and Λ=M hypotheses; it is not valid for a general measurable space.
gaps: No weak-topology compactness, tightness, or near-extremizer convergence is asserted.

constant_dependence.explicit: The support-size bound is the number k of generalized moment coordinates: an extreme point has at most k atomic partition pieces. There is no metric rate, radius, or concentration parameter.
constant_dependence.dependence: The literal Dirac support conclusion additionally depends on S being Polish with its Borel σ-algebra and Λ=M. The objective reduction depends on the extreme-point supremum condition and, for equality over feasible atom measures, Δ_f^(k)⊂Λ.

endpoint_limits.atomicity: On an abstract measurable space, conclusions are expressed via μ-atoms/partitions and finite atomic representatives; literal Dirac support requires Polish/Borel assumptions. If f includes the constant-one constraint, the representative also preserves total probability mass.
endpoint_limits.existence: Proposition 6 gives compactness of a maximizing face as one sufficient condition for an extreme maximizer; the paper does not establish such compactness for a new problem.
endpoint_limits.escape: No concentration-compactness alternative, tightness criterion for sequences, or mass-at-infinity analysis is provided.

reusable_methods.method: For an extreme point under k linear moment constraints, use a partition into more than k positive pieces to build a nontrivial moment-preserving signed perturbation; this forces at most k atomic pieces.
reusable_methods.transfer: The perturbation requires the feasible cone to be stable under restrictions and the moment integrals to be defined.

reusable_methods.method: When an objective maximum is attained at an extreme point, replace the optimizer by a measure supported on at most k points while preserving all constrained moments and the objective.
reusable_methods.transfer: Check the extreme-point attainment premise and whether finite-atom measures remain in the feasible cone.

reusable_methods.method: Use compactness of the maximizing face as one route to an extreme maximizer.
reusable_methods.transfer: This is a sufficient abstract condition, not a quantitative tightness estimate and not a guarantee that the face is compact.
